summary.intent: Monitor PR #349 for automated bot reviews (CodeRabbit, Copilot), auto-resolve them as they arrive, then collect staging performance baselines for the vault login path before a vault migration deploys.
summary.outcome: All 23 review threads across 4 rounds were resolved with real fixes (recovery IPNS name bug, getVault 404 scope, vault init conflict handling, zero-copy blob optimization). Staging perf baselines were captured. A session restore race condition was discovered, documented, and fixed with shared-Promise deduplication at two layers (auth/refresh and vault init).

repo: The cron/loop skill can be used to set up automated PR monitoring that fires /resolve-pr-reviews when new unresolved threads appear.
Outside-diff-range review comments don't surface as unresolved GraphQL reviewThreads — they must be fetched via the review body directly.
The vault key IPNS name and root folder IPNS name were previously conflated in recovery.html; PR #349 separated them.
VaultBlobV2 type was removed — functions now return Uint8Array directly.
E2E wallet login uses @johanneskares/wallet-mock with installMockWallet() for real secp256k1 signing via viem.
Core Kit DKG on Sapphire Devnet dominates login time (~9-45s); the vault-critical path is only ~700ms-1.4s.
Staging DB was wiped, so no existing vaults were present for baseline — the perf script had to create one first.

The Axios 401 interceptor in packages/api-client/src/instance.ts already deduplicates 401-triggered refreshes via refreshPromise, but direct authApi.refresh() calls (from session restore) are NOT covered.

code.finding: Broad try/catch around getVault() and all subsequent IPFS calls — a 404 from fetchFromIpfs (missing CID for existing vault) would incorrectly trigger vault re-initialization. Fixed by isolating getVault() in its own try/catch.
Session restore calls resolveIpnsRecord for vault key IPNS name; if record not found, throws 'Vault key IPNS name not found', which is caught at line 594 and triggers Core Kit logout.

Session restore effect calls authApi.refresh() directly — multiple React effect cycles can call this concurrently, bypassing the Axios interceptor deduplication. Root cause of the 6-concurrent-refresh-calls race.
Added module-level refreshPromise deduplication for direct authApi.refresh() calls to prevent concurrent session restore effects from each triggering a token refresh.
slice() was used instead of subarray() — slice copies the buffer, subarray returns a zero-copy view. Fixed to subarray().
sequence=0 conflict on IPNS publish was warn-and-continue; changed to abort with error to prevent partial vault state.
Axios 401 interceptor already deduplicates refresh via shared refreshPromise, but only for 401-triggered retries, not direct calls.

workflow: Playwright MCP browser_run_code runs in an ESM sandbox without Node module resolution — can't import local packages directly; use standalone .mjs scripts via Bash instead.
window.ethereum injection for Web3Auth wallet login must happen via addInitScript before page navigation, not via browser_evaluate after load.
Playwright native request/response events are more reliable for network monitoring across navigations than injected fetch monkey-patching.
The /loop skill creates a CronCreate job with recurring:true that auto-expires after 7 days.
GSD todos follow a specific markdown format with frontmatter; markdownlint enforces heading style and list formatting in CI.

friction: GitHub GraphQL API timed out once during the monitoring loop — transient network issue, no retry logic in the cron prompt.
Outside-diff-range comments don't surface as unresolved reviewThreads in the GraphQL query — required manual user intervention to notice them.
Playwright MCP browser_run_code can't resolve Node/npm modules, requiring a fallback to standalone scripts via Bash.
Web3Auth OTP on staging is real (not a test bypass), blocking direct MCP browser login flow.
The staging DB was wiped, meaning no live vaults existed for baseline measurement — had to create one first, adding an extra pass.
fetch monitoring injected via browser_evaluate didn't survive page navigation, requiring a rewrite to use Playwright's native request events.
Auth/refresh race condition caused 6 concurrent refresh calls on page reload, which fed into the vault init race — took significant log archaeology to trace the root cause.
open_items: Post-deploy re-measurement: run tests/web-e2e/staging-perf-wallet.mjs against staging after PR #349 deploys to get real IPNS resolve + IPFS fetch numbers for a v2 vault key blob.

The vault init deduplication guard added to useAuth.ts resets vaultInitPromise to null after completion — verify this handles the case where a second caller arrives while the first is in-flight vs after it completes.

No existing vaults on staging means the 'existing vault login' baseline (~1,379ms with two IPNS 404s) reflects the old code's double-resolve behavior; re-baseline after deploy to confirm the new single-resolve path.

The session restore test (scenario 3) couldn't be fully measured because Core Kit tKey shares don't persist across Playwright browser contexts — a proper session restore baseline requires a persistent browser profile or a Core Kit session mock.
The auth/refresh race fix and vault init fix are on fix/session-restore-race-conditions but not yet merged or PR'd.
